title: Unnecessary `metadata/_custom_type_script` saved in .tscn files
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.6.beta3.official [76dda5c6c] - Reproducible in v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee] - Reproducible in v4.4.dev5.official [9e6098432] - Reproducible in v4.4.dev4.official [36e6207bb] - Not reproducible in v4.4.dev3.official [f4af8201b] - Not reproducible in v4.4.dev2.official [97ef3c837] - Not reproducible in v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8] ### System information Godot v4.6.beta3 - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7680) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600KF (20 threads) - 47.84 GiB memory ### Issue description Why there are many `metadata/_custom_type_script` saved in .tscn files which seems unnecessary. Use Godot v4.3, create a scene with a custom node in it. Then use Godot v4.4/v4.5/v4.6 to open this scene, then do nothing but save it again, then we can see that the tscn file is not modified. Then delete the custom node then re-add this custom node and save it, then see the tscn file. The file is modified and added a meta data. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd9d97ee-a2f2-48fb-b09c-ca9e7d57d2d6 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use Godot v4.3.stable.official to open MRP. open the scene and save and check the tscn file with a text editor. 2. Use Godot v4.4.dev4.official to open MRP. open the scene and save and check the tscn file with a text editor. ---> File content not modified. 3. Use Godot v4.4.dev4.official to open MRP. open the scene and delete the custom node and re-add it and save and check the tscn file with a text editor. ---> file content modified. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [test-meta.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24549428/test-meta.zip)
